To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the stochastic gradient method with averaging and extrapolation can significantly outperform standard GAN training, while extrapolation from the previous step can outperform Adam.
the training of GANS is an example of a variational inequality, and that averaging, extrapolation, and extrapolation from thepast can be used to improve the performance of GANs.

(a) GAN optimization is not fundamentally harder than other optimization problems and can be solved with existing algorithms, and (b) the extrapolation methods are the most effective ones, especially in the context of Adam.

we show the potential of variational inequality solvers for training GANs and provide a toolbox of methods for practitioners.

the training of GANS is not fundamentally different from that of other machine learning problems, and that existing optimization techniques can be applied to improve training.
